Does the lack of power from subsonic ammo make a relevant difference when hitting game (or people)?

It, like so much else, depends on 1) Your aim & 2) What, exactly, you're hunting.

Squirrel? Dead. Rhino? Ooh, boy. You better run.

The only real, appreciable, differences are the decibels of the report and range of your shot. And range usually doesn't come into play unless you're shooting from a long distance off.

In the end, it almost doesn't matter. A bullet traveling at 1/2 the speed of sound is still surely going to fuck up most animals you'd normally hunt just as well as one doing 1.5x. Just won't penetrate as well.

I do have to add that when I've shot subsonic ammo in the past, the lower grain rounds had a substantially higher rate of jams. Not every shot, but enough to notice.

Less energy from muzzle means less energy going into the body, which means less expansion of the bullet, therefore less wound cavitation and thus a lower amount of damage.

Speed kills, as we have all heard.

Now, if you ten ring the MFer in the heart or brain, it likely won't matter just a whole lot to the guy getting shot, but any other area, I would want as much expansion and wound cavitation as possible, especially in a life or death situation where you need a one shot stop.

I don't have any sources I can cite for how much difference a subsonic round would be vs a full power round, unfortunately, and am only going off experience and horse sense. Manufacturers of high end bullets often will provide pics of their rounds recovered after an impact at 100 yards vs another at a much greater distance, and therefore slower bullet speed to show what kind of expansion the bullet gives at different velocities and the higher velocity bullet always expands more, said expansion being highly correlative with wound cavitation/wound channel size.

Remember that the larger the diameter of the projectile the faster it bleeds off velocity. The faster you bleed velocity the more parabolic arc you have in the flight of the projectile. This is why there is all the interest in small diameter but longer hyper velocity projectiles. The get there in a hurry (not as much time to fall toward the center of the earth, (remember gravity sucks), also less time to be affected by wind or air currents. The small diameter doesn't have the frontal area for air resistance and the long length give the bullet mass for the inertia. (A body a rest tends to remain at rest, and a body in motion tends to remain in motion in a straight line at a constant speed unless acted upon by an out side force) *outside force= gravity and air resistance.
